Rashi on Yevamot 10a:10:1.english: Even without "if" you can find [it] - that this deceased [man] did not transgress through marrying her.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:10:2.english: Raped his daughter-in-law - And transgressed the law.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:11:1.hebrew: ואע"פ - דמהדר ליה רבי ללוי, "כמדומה אני שאין לו מוח בקדקדו":
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:11:1.english: And even though - Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] responded to Levi, "It seems to me that he has no brain in his skull."

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:11:2.hebrew: בדקה לוי במתני' - הגיהה והוסיפה לאמו אנוסת אביו במשנתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:11:2.english: Levi established it in his mishnah - He emended it and added [the case of] his mother, the woman raped by his father, in his mishnah.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:12:1.hebrew: היתה אמו נשואת אביו ונשאת לאחיו מאביו ומת - לא תפסי קדושין בה, שהרי אשת אב בכרת, ואמרינן לקמן: אין קדושין תופסין בחייבי כריתות, דברי הכל. הלכך, כשמת רשע זה, לא נפלה זו לייבום לפני בנה, דלאו אשת אח הואי, ואינה פוטרת צרתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:12:1.english: His mother was married to his father, and she married his paternal brother, and [he] died - Betrothal does not take effect with her, for a father's wife is [a prohibition punishable by] karet, and we say later [in the tractate] that betrothal does not take effect with those liable to karet, according to all [opinions]. Therefore, when this wicked man died, this [woman] did not fall for levirate marriage before her son, because she was not [his] brother's wife, and [consequently] she does not exempt her rival wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:1:1.hebrew: וסמניך מת נולד ויבם כו' - כדפי'. אלמא, מדתני רבי חייא "בכולן אני קורא בהן", ואפילו באשת אחיו שלא היה בעולם, אלמא תנא דמתני' תני פלוגתא, דהא רבי חייא אמתני' קאי:
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:1:1.english: And your mnemonic [is]: Died, was born, and entered into levirate marriage, etc. - As I explained [above]. Thus, since Rabbi Ḥiyya taught: "To all of them I apply [this rule]," even to the wife of his brother who was not [yet] in the world, it follows that the Tanna of the Mishnah taught a disputed [ruling], for Rabbi Ḥiyya is referring to the Mishnah.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:2:1.hebrew: לרבי לית ליה הני כללי - דר' חייא. הלכך, לא מוקמי מתני' בפלוגתא, אלא בנולד ולבסוף ייבם לדברי הכל:
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:2:1.english: Rabbi does not hold [in accordance with] these general statements - of Rabbi Ḥiyya. Therefore, they do not establish the Mishnah as [referring to] a dispute, rather [as referring] to [a case where] he was born and afterward he performed levirate marriage, according to all [opinions].

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:2:2.hebrew: אמו אנוסת אביו בחדא משכחת לה - להכי לא נקט לה במתני', שאי אתה קורא בה "האסורה לזה מותרת לזה, ואחותה כשהיא יבמתה מתייבמת" — שיהו ב' אחיות נופלות להתייבם, ותהא זו אסורה לזה משום אמו, וכן זו על זה, ומותרת לשני — אלא חדא משכחת לה, או "האסורה לזה מותרת לזה", או "אחותה כשהיא יבמתה":
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:2:2.english: His mother, [who was] raped by his father, you find [this] in one [case] - Therefore [the Tanna] did not mention her in the Mishnah, because you cannot apply to her [both]: "She who is forbidden to this one is permitted to that one, and her sister, when she is her sister-in-law, is taken in levirate marriage" — [meaning] that two sisters should fall for levirate marriage, and this one be forbidden to this [brother] because of "his mother," and likewise this [other] one to that [other brother], while [each is] permitted to the second [brother] — rather, you find [only] one [of them]: either "She who is forbidden to this one is permitted to that one," or "Her sister, when she is her sister-in-law."

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:3:1.hebrew: אי יעקב שתי אחיות אנס - וילדה לו האחת לוי והאחת יהודה, ונשא ראובן אנוסת אביו, אמו של לוי, ושמעון נשא אנוסת אביו, אמו של יהודה:
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:3:1.english: If Jacob raped two sisters - And one bore him Levi and the other [bore him] Judah, and Reuven married his father's rape victim, the mother of Levi, and Shimon married his father's rape victim, the mother of Judah.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:3:2.hebrew: אחותה כשהיא יבמתה - נופלת לייבום לפני לוי ויהודה בניה, משכחת לה:
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:3:2.english: Her sister when she is her sister-in-law - [When she] falls for levirate marriage before Levi and Yehudah, her sons, you find it.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:3:3.hebrew: האסורה לזה מותרת לזה לא משכחת לה - לפי ששתיהן אסורות על שניהם: אמו של לוי אסורה לו משום אמו, ואחותה משום אחות האם, וכן ליהודה. ושתיהן פטורות מן החליצה ומן הייבום:
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:3:3.english: She who is forbidden to this one is permitted to that one, you cannot find it - Because both [women] are forbidden to both of them: Levi's mother is forbidden to him on account of [being] his mother, and her sister on account of [being] his mother's sister, and likewise for Yehudah. Thus, both of them are exempt from chalitzah and from yibum.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:4:1.hebrew: ואי שתי נכריות אנס - וילדו לו ב' בנים, ונשאום ב' בנים מאשה אחרת, ונפלו לפני בניהם, האסורה לזה מותרת לזה משכחת לה, אבל לאו אחיות נינהו. ועיקר מילתיה דרבי חייא משום ייבום שתי אחיות נקט:
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:4:1.english: And if he raped two unrelated women - and they bore him two sons, and two [other] sons from another wife married them, and they fell [for levirate marriage] before their sons — [the case of] "she who is forbidden to this one is permitted to that one" is found, but they are not sisters. And the main [point of] Rabbi Ḥiyya's statement was taught regarding the levirate marriage of two sisters.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:5:1.hebrew: ה"ג רב אשי אמר לעולם לית ליה לר' הני כללי ובפלוגתא קא מיירי - כלומר, לא תימא דהא דלא תני אמו אנוסת אביו משום דלא משכחת [בה] הני כללי, דלרבי ל"ל הני כללי; ולא תימא להכי שבקיה דלא מיירי בפלוגתא, דבפלוגתא ודאי קמיירי. ומאי "אין לו מוח" דקאמר ליה — ה"ק ליה כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:5:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: Rav Ashi said: Actually, Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] does not hold these general rules, and it deals with a dispute - That is to say, do not say that the reason [the Mishnah] does not teach [the case of] his mother who was violated by his father is because these general rules are not found [to apply] to it, for Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] does not hold these general rules; and do not say that for this reason he omitted it—that he does not deal with a dispute—for he certainly does deal with a dispute. And what [is the meaning of] "he has no brain" that he said to him? This is what he is saying to him, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:6:1.english: Who prohibited [the case of] a woman raped by one’s father - And [therefore] you do not find [a case] in which a mother falls before her son for levirate marriage from his brother or from his father.

Rashi on Yevamot 10a:9:1.hebrew: דאי עבר ונסיב - את אנוסת אביו, ונפלה לייבום לפני בנה, וליתני:
Rashi on Yevamot 10a:9:1.english: That if one transgressed and married - the woman raped by his father, and she fell for levirate marriage before her son, let [the Mishnah] teach [this case]!

Tosafot on Yevamot 10a:5:1.hebrew: לעולם לית ליה לרבי הני כללי ובפלוגתא קמיירי - וא"ת: ליתני אשת איש שפוטרת צרתה, כגון דאמר לה: ה"ז גיטך ע"מ שלא תנשאי לפלוני, דפליגי בהמגרש (גיטין דף פב.) ר"א ורבנן, דלר"א הוי גט ואסורה לפלוני, ואם נשאת לאחיו ומת — פוטרת צרתה. ואע"ג דאסורה לכל אדם אפי' לרבי אליעזר מדרבנן עד שימות המגרש או הפלוני, דחיישינן שמא תנשא לו לאחר שתתאלמן או תתגרש מזה ונמצאו בניה ממזרים, כדחיישינן בהמגרש (שם דף פד.) ע"מ שלא תבעלי לפלוני, שמא תבעל לו אחר שתתאלמן או אחר שתתגרש, ובעודה תחתיו ליכא למיחש יותר מאבא ואביך — מ"מ לוי, דקתני נמי דאי כדאמרינן לקמן, קשה: דליתני נמי להך! ולמאן דנפקא ליה מאחות אשה ניחא, דלא דמי הך לאחות אשה: דע"מ שלא תנשאי — שריא ליה בזנות, וע"מ שלא תבעלי — יכולה היא להתקדש לו, ולא דמיא לאחות אשה. ובע"מ שלא תנשאי ולא תבעלי נמי: אי חשיב שיור כמו בחוץ מפלוני, א"כ שריא ליה כי נשאת לאחיו קודם; ואפי' אי לא חשיב שיור, מ"מ לא דמי לאחות אשה, דהתם בשעת נפילה הוי אחות אשתו, אבל הכא בשעת נפילה אינה אשת איש עד שתבעל לו. ואפי' תחשבנה אשת איש, כיון שמטעם אשת איש אסורה ליבעל לו, מ"מ לא דמי: כיון שאם תבעל ליבם שנאסרה עליו הויא אשת איש ולא היתה אשת אחיו מעולם, הלכך לא פטרה צרתה. ומיהו למאן דנפקא ליה מולקחה כל היכא דאיכא תרי ליקוחין — קשה. וי"ל: אע"ג דלוי תני דאי ובפלוגתא קמיירי, לא קמיירי אלא בפלוגתא דס"ל לתנא דמתני' כוותיה. תדע, דלא תני לוי חייבי לאוין, אע"ג דלר"ע לאו בני חליצה וייבום נינהו. ומאן דמוסיף לעיל אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, ומשכחת לה כר"ש אע"ג דשמא תנא דמתני לא סבר לה כר"ש — היינו משום דבכולן "אני קורא בהן" משמע ליה דקאי אכולהו. אבל אי מודו רבנן לר"א בקידושין — דמספקא ליה לאביי מדקאמר בריש המגרש (גיטין דף פב: ושם) דאם איתא לר' אבא קשיא — ליתני אשת איש, דמשכחת לה אפילו לרבנן, כגון שבא ראובן וקדשה חוץ משמעון, ובא שמעון וקדשה סתם, ומת שמעון [ונפלה לפני לוי אחיו]; וצרת צרה נמי משכחת לה, כגון שקדשה ראובן חוץ משני אחין. וי"ל: דלא קרינא לגביה אשת המת, דכבר נאסרה [עליו לפני קדושי אחים] משום אשת [אח], ולא חשיב ערוה במקום מצוה. ומיהו אי אשת שני מתים דאורייתא, כדמשמע בהמגרש (שם דף פב: ושם), ליתני הכא אשת ב' מתים, כגון שבא ראובן וקדשה חוץ משמעון ולוי אחיו, ובא שמעון וקדשה סתם ומת כו', או בענין שאמר ר' יוחנן בפ' האומר (קדושין דף ס.) דאפילו הן ק' תופסין, ומשכחת בהן נמי צרת צרה! ומיהו בפ"ג (לקמן יבמות לא: ושם ד"ה מדרבנן) ובפ"ב (לקמן יבמות יח. ושם) משמע דאשת שני מתים גזירה דרבנן, ושם אפרש. ובירושלמי בריש המגרש פריך לה: מתיב ר' חנינא בשם רבי פנחס: ליתני ט"ז נשים כר"א! ומשני: תמן התורה אסרה עליו, הכא הוא אסרה עליו. ופי' רבינו יצחק: תמן התורה אסרה עליו, ומשנשאה המת אין לה היתר להתייבם כשימות, מפני שאין איסור שבה תלוי בשום אדם אלא בתורה שאסרה עליו; אבל אשת איש — האיסור תלוי במגרש, שאם ירצה יתירנה ליבם קודם שימות אחיו שנשאה. ולהכי לא תני להו, דלא דמו להו, לפי שביד המגרש להתירה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 10a:5:1.english: Actually, Rabbi does not hold these general statements, and [the Mishnah] does deal with a dispute - And if you ask: Let [the Tanna] teach a married woman who exempts her co-wife! For example, where [her husband] said to her, "Behold, this is your bill of divorce on condition that you do not marry so-and-so," regarding which Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages disagree in [chapter] HaMegaresh (Gittin 82a): for according to Rabbi Eliezer it is a valid bill of divorce and she is forbidden to so-and-so, and if she [subsequently] married his brother and [the brother] died, she exempts her co-wife. And even though she is forbidden to every man even according to Rabbi Eliezer by rabbinic decree until the divorcer or that so-and-so dies — since we are concerned lest she marry [so-and-so] after she is widowed or divorced from this [second husband], and her children would be found to be mamzerim, just as we are concerned in HaMegaresh (ibid., 84a) [in the case of] "on condition that you do not cohabit with so-and-so," lest she cohabit with him after she is widowed or after she is divorced, whereas while she is still under [her second husband] there is no reason to be concerned any more than [in the case of] "my father or your father" — nevertheless, [according to] Levi, who also teaches [cases of] "if" as we say later, it is difficult: let him teach this [case] as well! And according to the one who derives [the law of co-wives] from "a woman's sister" [i.e., "to be a rival to her"], it is well, for this [case] is not comparable to a woman's sister: for [in the case of] "on condition that you do not marry [so-and-so]," she is permitted to him through non-marital intercourse; and [in the case of] "on condition that you do not cohabit [with him]," she is able to become betrothed to him — so it is not comparable to a woman's sister. And even [in the case of] "on condition that you neither marry nor cohabit [with him]": if it is considered a reservation [in the divorce], like "except for so-and-so," then she is permitted to him if she married his brother first; and even if it is not considered a reservation, nevertheless it is not comparable to a woman's sister, for there at the time of falling [for levirate marriage] she is his wife's sister, whereas here at the time of falling she is not a married woman until she cohabits with him. And even if you consider her a married woman, since by reason of being a married woman she is forbidden to cohabit with him, nevertheless it is not comparable: since if she cohabits with the levir [the condition is violated and] she was retroactively forbidden to him, she is a married woman and was never his brother's wife at all; therefore she does not exempt her co-wife. However, according to the one who derives it from "and take her" — wherever there are two "takings" [i.e., valid marriages], it is difficult. And one can answer: Even though Levi teaches [cases of] "if" and deals with disputes, he only deals with a dispute where the Tanna of our Mishnah holds like him. Know that this is so, for Levi does not teach those forbidden by negative commandments, even though according to Rabbi Akiva they are not subject to chalitzah or levirate marriage. And as for the one who adds above "the wife of his brother who was not in his world," which is found [to exempt her co-wife] according to Rabbi Shimon even though perhaps the Tanna of the Mishnah does not hold like Rabbi Shimon — that is because since in all of them [the wording] "I apply to them" [is used], it seems to him that it refers to all of them. But if the Sages concede to Rabbi Eliezer regarding betrothal — which Abaye is uncertain about, as he says at the beginning of HaMegaresh (Gittin 82b and ibid.) that if Rabbi Abba's [statement] is correct, it is difficult — let [the Mishnah] teach a married woman, which is found even according to the Sages: for example, where Reuven came and betrothed her "except for Shimon," and Shimon came and betrothed her unconditionally, and Shimon died [and she fell before Levi his brother]; and a co-wife's co-wife is also found, for example, where Reuven betrothed her "except for two brothers." And one can answer: We do not apply to him [the term] "wife of the deceased," for she was already forbidden [to him before the brothers' betrothal] on account of "a [brother's] wife," and she is not considered a forbidden relative in a place of a mitzvah. However, if "the wife of two deceased [husbands]" is biblical, as implied in HaMegaresh (ibid., 82b and ibid.), let [the Mishnah] teach here "the wife of two deceased [husbands]," for example, where Reuven came and betrothed her "except for Shimon and Levi his brother," and Shimon came and betrothed her unconditionally and died, etc., or in the manner that Rabbi Yochanan said in chapter HaOmer (Kiddushin 60a), that even if there are one hundred [such betrothals], they take effect, and among them a co-wife's co-wife is also found! However, in the third chapter (below, Yevamot 31b, and ibid., s.v. "miderabbanan") and in the second chapter (below, Yevamot 18a and ibid.), it is implied that "the wife of two deceased [husbands]" is a rabbinic decree, and there I will explain. And in the Yerushalmi, at the beginning of HaMegaresh, it raises this objection: Rabbi Chanina objected in the name of Rabbi Pinchas: Let it teach sixteen women according to Rabbi Eliezer! And it answers: There, the Torah forbade her to him; here, he forbade her to himself. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak explained: There, the Torah forbade her to him, and once the deceased married her she has no [possibility of] becoming permitted to enter levirate marriage when he dies, because her prohibition does not depend on any person, but rather on the Torah that forbade her to him; whereas [for] a married woman [in the conditional divorce case], the prohibition depends on the divorcer, for if he wishes he can permit her to the levir before his brother who married her dies. And therefore [the Mishnah] does not teach them, for they are not comparable to them, since it is in the power of the divorcer to permit her.

Tosafot on Yevamot 10a:7:1.hebrew: דקתני שש עריות חמורות מאלו כו' - ותימה: דמאי ס"ד דהנהו דלעיל דלא דייקי מסיפא? וממ"נ, כיון דתני לה גבי שש עריות, לא אפשר למיתנייה ברישא! וי"ל דקשיא ליה ללוי דה"ל למיתני ברישא ט"ז ובסיפא לא הוה ליה למיתני אלא ה'; ואע"ג דאתי כרבי יהודה, ה"ל למיתני ששה עשר דאי עבר ונסיב, ושני ליה רבי: בפלוגתא לא קא מיירי — ודאי לא קא מיירי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 10a:7:1.english: "As it teaches: Six forbidden relations are more severe than these, etc." - And it is astonishing: what was the assumption of those [Amoraim] above, who did not infer from the latter clause [that the mishna follows Rabbi Yehuda]? In any event, since [the mishna] teaches her among the six forbidden relations, it is impossible to teach her in the first clause! And one can answer that Levi's difficulty was that [the mishna] should have taught sixteen in the first clause and in the latter clause it should only have taught five; and even though it follows Rabbi Yehuda, it should have taught sixteen, [on the grounds] that if [the brother] transgressed and married [her, she would exempt her rival wife], and Rabbi answered him: "It does not deal with a matter of dispute" — [and in that respect] it certainly does not deal [with a matter of dispute].

Tosafot on Yevamot 10a:9:1.hebrew: לרבי יהודה נמי משכחת לה דאי עבר ונסיב - תימה, דבלא "דאי עבר ונסיב" נמי משכחת לה, שקידש ולא בעל; דאפילו אביי דאמר בפרק בתרא דקידושין (דף עח.) גבי אלמנה לכ"ג "קידש — לוקה", היינו משום דכתיב "לא יקח", אבל הכא "לא יגלה" כתיב. וי"ל, דשמא אסור לקדש מדרבנן, שמא יבעול; ואפילו יהא מותר לקדשה, חשיב "דאי" מטעם שאסור לבוא עליה. וא"ת: אפילו ע"י "דאי", היכי משכחת לה? הא ר' יהודה סבר כר"ע בפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נג.), דאמר אין קדושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין! וי"ל, דלא סבר לה הש"ס כברייתא דהתם, אלא כמתני' דפליג עלה. ועוד, דעל כרחך מתני' דהכא לא סברה בהא כרבי יהודה, דהא קתני בפ"ב (לקמן יבמות דף כ.): "איסור מצוה ואיסור קדושה חולצת ולא מתייבמת", ואי אין קדושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין, חליצה נמי לא תיבעי! וא"ת: בחייבי לאוין דשאר מנלן דלא סבר מתני' כרבי יהודה? ד"איסור מצוה ואיסור קדושה" מפרש לקמן כגון אלמנה לכ"ג, גרושה וחלוצה לכהן הדיוט, ממזרת ונתינה לישראל. ואר"י, דע"כ מתני' סבר דאפי' בחייבי לאוין דשאר קידושין תופסין, מדקתני שש עריות ולא קתני ח' עריות — גרושתו וחלוצתו; דאם היו יכולות לינשא לאחיו, היו פוטרות צרותיהן כחייבי כריתות, כיון דאין קידושין תופסין! אלא ודאי קידושין תופסין בהו, ולהכי לא שייך למיתנינהו, דאפי' היו יכולות לינשא לאחיו, לא היו פוטרות צרותיהן. ועוד יש לדקדק, מדנקט "אנוסת אביו שהיא אמו", ולא נקט "אנוסת אביו" סתם. וא"ת: כיון דמתני' סבר כרבי יהודה דאסר באנוסת אביו, א"כ ע"כ סבר נמי דאין קידושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין, דהא בהא תליא! כדמוכח בסוף החולץ (לקמן יבמות דף מט. ושם), דמפרש טעמא דר"ע דאמר "יש ממזר מחייבי לאוין" משום דסבר לה כרבי יהודה, דמוקי "לא יגלה" באנוסת אביו וסמיך ליה "לא יבא ממזר"; וא"כ למתני' נמי הוי ממזר, וכל היכא דהוי ממזר — אין קידושין תופסין, כדמוכח בכמה דוכתי. וי"ל, דאע"ג דמתני' מוקמה לקרא באנוסת אביו, מ"מ לא הוי ממזר; כמו לרבי יהושע דמוקי "לא יגלה" בשומרת יבם של אביו, אפ"ה סבר דלא הוי ממזר אלא מחייבי מיתות ב"ד, ודרשינן: מ"לא יקח" דהוי חייבי מיתות ב"ד עד "לא יגלה" דהוי חייבי כריתות הוי ממזר, ולא חייבי כריתות. וה"נ לתנא דמתני': מ"לא יקח" עד "לא יגלה" שהוא חייבי לאוין הוי ממזר, ולא חייבי לאוין בכלל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 10a:9:1.english: Even according to Rabbi Yehuda you can find this [case] — what if he transgressed and married - It is astonishing, for even without "what if he transgressed and married" you can find it, [namely] where he betrothed [her] and did not cohabit [with her]; for even Abaye, who says in the last chapter of Kiddushin (78a) regarding a widow to a High Priest [that if] "he betrothed — he receives lashes," that is because it is written "he shall not take," whereas here "he shall not uncover" is written. And one can answer that perhaps it is prohibited to betroth [her] by rabbinic decree, lest he cohabit [with her]; and even if it were permitted to betroth her, it is considered "what if" because it is prohibited to cohabit with her. And if you say: Even by way of "what if," how can you find it? Does not Rabbi Yehuda hold like Rabbi Akiva in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 53a), who says that betrothal does not take effect with those liable for negative prohibitions? And one can answer that the Gemara does not hold like that baraita there, rather like the Mishnah [there] that disagrees with it. Furthermore, perforce our Mishnah here does not hold like Rabbi Yehuda in this [matter], for it teaches in the second chapter (below, Yevamot 20a): "[A woman forbidden by] a prohibition of a mitzvah or a prohibition of sanctity performs chalitzah and does not enter levirate marriage," and if betrothal does not take effect with those liable for negative prohibitions, she should not require chalitzah either! And if you say: Regarding those liable for negative prohibitions of kinship, from where do we know that the Mishnah does not hold like Rabbi Yehuda? For "a prohibition of a mitzvah and a prohibition of sanctity" is explained below [to refer to cases] such as a widow to a High Priest, a divorcee or a chalutzah to an ordinary priest, [and] a mamzeret or a netinah to an Israelite. And Rabbi Yitzchak says that perforce the Mishnah holds that even with those liable for negative prohibitions of kinship, betrothal takes effect, from the fact that it teaches six forbidden relations and does not teach eight forbidden relations — [adding] his divorcee [after remarrying another] and his chalutzah; for [if betrothal did not take effect with them, then] if they were able to marry his brother, they would exempt their co-wives like those liable for karet, since betrothal does not take effect! Rather, certainly betrothal takes effect with them, and therefore it is not relevant to teach them, since even if they were able to marry his brother, they would not exempt their co-wives. And furthermore, one can infer [this] from the fact that it states "his father's rape victim who is his mother," and does not state "his father's rape victim" unqualifiedly. And if you say: Since the Mishnah holds like Rabbi Yehuda, who prohibits his father's rape victim, if so, perforce it also holds that betrothal does not take effect with those liable for negative prohibitions, for the one depends on the other! As is evident at the end of [the chapter] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 49a and there), where [the Gemara] explains the reason of Rabbi Akiva, who says "a mamzer is produced from those liable for negative prohibitions," because he holds like Rabbi Yehuda, who establishes "he shall not uncover" as referring to his father's rape victim, and juxtaposed to it is "a mamzer shall not enter"; and if so, according to the Mishnah as well [the offspring] is a mamzer, and wherever [the offspring] is a mamzer — betrothal does not take effect, as is evident in several places. And one can answer that even though the Mishnah establishes the verse as referring to his father's rape victim, nevertheless [the offspring] is not a mamzer; just as according to Rabbi Yehoshua, who establishes "he shall not uncover" as referring to his father's yevamah awaiting levirate marriage, even so he holds that [an offspring] is a mamzer only from those liable for court-imposed death penalties, and we expound: from "he shall not take," which is [among] those liable for court-imposed death penalties, up to "he shall not uncover," which is [among] those liable for karet, [the offspring] is a mamzer, and not [from] those liable for karet [themselves]. And so too according to the Tanna of our Mishnah: from "he shall not take" up to "he shall not uncover," which is [among] those liable for negative prohibitions, [the offspring] is a mamzer, and those liable for negative prohibitions [themselves] are not included:
